page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for workloads requiring high local storage capacity and low latency. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with 4 vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory and a dedicated 950 GB NVMe SSD local storage drive. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, operating under a Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that the compute and memory subsystems operate on the lower end of the performance spectrum. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 10% category. Memory bandwidth tests also show weak to poor performance, with large block read-only speeds at 22.62 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.23 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is measured at 2.81 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% of tested instances.

The primary value proposition of the i3.xlarge lies in its local NVMe SSD storage capacity rather than raw processing power. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a dense storage-to-resource ratio, making it suitable for storage-bound applications that do not require intensive CPU or memory throughput. The clear tradeoff is the lower-tier compute and memory performance relative to modern general-purpose instances. Consequently, the i3.xlarge is best suited for workloads such as localized databases, NoSQL data stores, transactional caches, and basic data warehousing where high-speed local storage capacity is the primary bottleneck.
